title.title: One-sample matroid prophet inequalities
title.subtitle: Claim: one past sample per element earns a constant fraction of the optimum on every matroid

plain: Accept or reject offers as they arrive, having seen only one past example of each: you still win a fixed share

beats.text: A small instance: edges arrive one at a time; keep any set with no cycle
The rule has seen one past sample per edge, and must accept or reject on the spot
Claimed: a constant share of the prophet's optimum, even against an almighty adversary

steps: Treat the past samples as values the rule gives up
Group the values by size, low to high
Build nested sets and pick greedily, layer by layer
Nesting keeps the picks allowed in any arrival order

data.result: a fixed share in any order

achievement.label: Does one sample per element give a constant on every matroid?
achievement.context: Before: $1/2$ with known distributions (Kleinberg–Weinberg, 2012); one sample lost $O(\log\log \text{rank})$
achievement.note: The constant $2^{-310}$ is existential; no efficient implementation is claimed

verify.ourCheck: We did not build the Lean or referee the proof

voice.text: Offers arrive one by one, in the worst order. You saw one past example of each.
Values are grouped by size and picked greedily in nested layers.
Claimed: a fixed share, though tiny.

sources.quote: achieves expected reward >= 2^{-310} E[OPT] on every finite matroid
Kleinberg-Weinberg (2012) 1/2 for matroids with known distributions
order-oblivious matroid secretary with O(log log rank) loss giving one-sample guarantees with that loss
Constant 2^{-310} is purely existential; no polynomial-time or oracle-efficient implementation is asserted.
main theorem formalized: MatroidProphet.lean and MatroidSecretary.lean, standard axioms
